procedural_matters: The hearing was conducted by a panel under N1.4(b).

On Aug. 1, a previously unknown video of the incident taken from the Race Committee vessel was provided to GRE 225861 who requested to reopen case 8 (case 25). Case 25 found that the new video evidence is significant evidence.
In case 25, the protest committee decided to reopen the hearing.
facts: The wind was 12-14 knots with 1 meter waves.
45 seconds before the start, ITA 226609 was on starboard immediately behind the Race Committee vessel.
Four boats, also on starboard, were abeam of him to leeward, the boat immediately to leeward to him was CRO.
40 seconds before the start, ITA 226609 drifted to leeward and made contact with the starboard side of the CRO.
30 seconds before the start, ITA 226609 luffed and a space of 1 ½ boat widths was created between ITA 226609 and CRO.
CRO bore off and the space increased.
GRE 225861 was on starboard astern and to leeward of ITA 226609.
GRE 225861 sailed into the space between ITA 226609 and CRO which was now of one boat length.
15 seconds before the start, ITA 226609 bore off 30 degrees and touched the Race Committee safety buoy.
10 seconds before the start, ITA 226609 continued to bear off and made contact with the starboard side transom of GRE 225861.
5 seconds before the start, ITA 226609 luffed to close-hauled and detached from GRE 225861.
At go, ITA 226609 stalled and started race 3 clear astern of GRE 225862 and the line of other boats starting.
30 seconds after the start, ITA 226609 did one tack and one gybe two boat lengths in front of the Race Committee vessel.
conclusions: ITA 226609 to windward failed to keep clear of CRO to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
ITA 226609 did not avoid contact with CRO even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14 (a).
It was not reasonably possible for CRO to avoid ITA 226609 when it became clear that ITA 226609 was not keeping clear. CRO did not break RRS 14(a).
ITA 226609 touched a mark at broke RRS 31.
ITA 226609 to windward failed to keep clear of GRE 225861 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
ITA 226609 did not avoid contact with GRE 225861 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14 (a).
It was not reasonably possible for GRE 225861 to avoid ITA 226609 when it became clear that ITA 226609 was not keeping clear. GRE 225861 did not break RRS 14(a).
ITA 226609 took an applicable penalty for breaking RRS 31, but did not take an applicable penalty for breaking RRS 11, 14(a).
